text:
maya: ACME escalation 1: they need SSO + tenant provisioning to run the pilot. Sales (anya) wants it in public v1. We need a decision today 1.

anya: Theyre willing to sign an SOW for early access but will push for it in v1 otherwise. Theyre a key reference and want audit evidence.

jordan: Quick infra reality check: end-to-end SSO (SAML + OIDC) + org provisioning touches auth, routing, audit logs, and provisioning APIs 1. Ballpark: 2.51-3.5w build + 1w security/compliance review, assuming no major blockers.

sam: From UX: we can deliver a limited experience faster: placeholder SSO screens + a migration UX, but it wont meet enterprise audit needs (no SSO attestation).

lee: Ops fallback: manual onboarding/runbook for 1 customer is doable for a few weeks. Not scalable. Also adds runbook ops burden and on-call risk.

maya: Options on table:
- Option A: Keep public v1 as-is (core inference + simple tenant routing). Offer ACME a paid SOW (early SSO) and a dedicated pilot lane.
- Option B: Fold SSO into public v1 -> shift v1 ~2w and expand QA/compliance window.
- Option C: Ship degraded SSO (basic connection without audit pack) in v1, deliver audit evidence later.

jordan: Engineering prefers A. It isolates schedule risk and keeps milestone. If we do C we still need a compliance sprint right after v1 which effectively shifts post-launch work.

sam: UX prefers A or C (A reduces QA scope; C is confusing for customers unless we label it "experimental SSO").

maya: Proposed compromise: Adopt Option A + feature-flagged pilot path. Work for ACME under SOW; we enable a pilot-only feature flag for SSO that can be toggled per-tenant on Dedicated or Private deployments. That lets ACME test earlier without moving v1.

lee: If we go feature-flag route we must add a canary rollback plan and a short runbook for manual backout. Ops can support that for an SOW customer.

jordan: I can draft an RFC with task-level breakdown and a feature-flag implementation plan by EOD tomorrow. Will include rollback matrix and test checklist.

sam: Ill mock the "experimental SSO" UX + migration notes and a short comms blurb for customer-facing docs by Wed.

anya: Ill confirm with ACME if they prefer earlier SSO under an SOW (paid onboarding + limited SLA) vs. waiting for v1. If they take SOW, were good with pilot-only feature flag. Also discussing pilot credits as a concession.

maya: Also need product-legal signoff on SOW terms (data handling + compliance evidence SLA). Tagging product-legal in follow-up.

ops-bot: Meeting created: "ACME onboarding SOW vs v1 decision" 2026-03-25 11:00 PT. Invite: @maya @jordan @sam @lee @anya.

maya: Quick mitigation checklist (draft):
```
MVP (public v1):
- core inference API
- basic tenant routing (API-key per tenant)
- telemetry, cost gating, canary rollouts

Pilot-SOW (ACME):
- SSO (SAML/OIDC) behind tenant-level feature flag
- org provisioning + role mapping (pilot only)
- onboarding runbook + ops backout steps
- compliance evidence pack delivered as part of SOW
- pilot credits/discount negotiated by sales
```

lee: +1 for checklist. Need explicit SLA on how long ops will support manual fallback. Put that in runbook.

jordan: Action items summary:
- jordan: RFC & task estimate by EOD tomorrow (includes rollback + tests)
- sam: UX mocks + migration doc by Wed
- lee: ops runbook draft for manual onboarding/backout by Fri
- anya: confirm ACME acceptance of SOW vs v1 by EOD tomorrow
- maya: loop in product-legal and update milestone tracker if we shift course

maya: Quick vote: react with :thumbsup: to keep v1 date + SOW/pilot-flag approach, :thumbsdown: to fold SSO into public v1 and delay.

jordan: :thumbsup:

sam: :thumbsup:

lee: :thumbsup: (ops okay with temporary support if SOW)

anya: :thumbsup: (sales will push SOW first)

maya: Consensus is to keep v1 and pursue SOW pilot with feature flag. Ill update the milestone tracker after jordan's RFC. Thanks all.
